# MANTIS-Std — Standard Test Cases for MANTIS-Sim

**Dataset version 1.0.0** · generated by the MANTIS-Sim emulator v0.2 (`software/v0.1.1/emulator`)

A small, frozen set of simulated unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) flyovers of a ground sensor field. Each case holds the time series that every sensor node recorded, the microphone audio and the upward fisheye camera frames, together with the exact ground truth. Use it to develop and compare detection, localization, tracking, and sensor-fusion algorithms without running the simulator.

Every case is generated from a fixed specification with a fixed random seed, so everyone on the team works from identical data and results are directly comparable.

---

```
standard_testcases/
```

## The six cases

All cases share one field so results line up: **6 nodes on a 50 m ring** centered on the origin, **24 s** of data, audio at **8000 Hz**, camera at **1 frame per second (fps)** (25 frames), **240 × 240** monochrome fisheye with a **185°** field of view (FOV), clear day sky, **15 dB** signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Each case changes one thing relative to the TC01 baseline.

| ID | Name | Airframe | Flight | Altitude | Speed | Closest slant range | ≈ Peak span on camera |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **TC01** | `overhead_pass` | SWIFT-UAV fixed wing | Straight, (−300, 0) → (300, 0) m, over nodes 1 and 4 | 80 m | 25.0 m/s | 79.9 m | 2.4 px |
| **TC02** | `offset_pass` | SWIFT-UAV | Straight, (−300, 120) → (300, 120) m, 70 m outside the ring | 80 m | 25.0 m/s | 110.7 m | 1.7 px |
| **TC03** | `loiter` | SWIFT-UAV | One counterclockwise circle, radius 80 m, centered on the array, starts on +x | 80 m | 20.9 m/s | 85.3 m | 2.3 px |
| **TC04** | `low_pass` | SWIFT-UAV | Same track as TC01 | 30 m | 25.0 m/s | 29.9 m | 6.5 px |
| **TC05** | `f550_pass` | F550-class hexacopter | Straight, (−120, 0) → (120, 0) m | 40 m | 10.0 m/s | 39.9 m | 1.5 px |
| **TC06** | `degraded_pass` | SWIFT-UAV | TC01 with **nodes 2 and 5 offline** (microphone and camera) | 80 m | 25.0 m/s | 79.9 m | 2.4 px |

The last column is a planning estimate from the emulator's pixel range budget (full airframe span, equidistant lens). The exact per-frame values are in `truth.camera.pixelArea` and `truth.camera.bbox`. Most cases put the target at only a few pixels, so the visual channel behaves as a bearing-only point detector; TC04 is the one case where the airframe is clearly resolved.

### Node layout

Node 1 sits on +x and numbering runs counterclockwise every 60°:

| Node | x (m) | y (m) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 50.0 | 0.0 |
| 2 | 25.0 | 43.3 |
| 3 | −25.0 | 43.3 |
| 4 | −50.0 | 0.0 |
| 5 | −25.0 | −43.3 |
| 6 | 25.0 | −43.3 |

Microphones are on the ground ($z = 0$); cameras are 0.15 m above them, looking straight up.

## Generating the dataset

Requires MATLAB (no toolboxes) and the MANTIS-Sim repository.

```matlab
cd('<repo>/datasets/standard_testcases')
make_standard_testcases();       % about a minute; writes MANTIS-Std-v1.0.0/
verify_standard_testcases();     % should print "6 of 6 case(s) passed."
```

The generator finds the emulator at `../../software/v0.1.1/emulator` automatically. If your copy lives elsewhere:

```matlab
make_standard_testcases('emulatorDir', 'C:\path\to\software\v0.1.1\emulator');
```

Other options: `'cases', {'TC01','TC04'}` builds a subset, `'overwrite', true` replaces existing files, `'previews', false` skips the PNG plots. Run `verify_standard_testcases('regenerate', true)` to rebuild every case from the specification and report how far it drifts from the saved files (zero on the same MATLAB and emulator version).

---

## File format

Each `TCxx_*.mat` is a **MAT v7** file (compressed, not HDF5) with six top-level structs. MATLAB reads it with `load`; Python reads it with `scipy.io.loadmat` or the included `mantis_std.py`. Sizes below use $T = 192\,001$ audio samples, $K = 25$ frames, $N = 6$ nodes, $H = W = 240$ pixels.

### `info` — identification and provenance

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `caseId`, `slug`, `title`, `description` | Case identity |
| `dataset`, `datasetVersion` | `MANTIS-Std`, `1.0.0` |
| `simulator`, `simulatorPath`, `simulatorCommit` | Emulator version string, folder, and Git commit when available |
| `generatedUTC`, `matlabVersion` | When and with what it was generated |
| `platformName` | Airframe display name |
| `coordinateFrame`, `units`, `indexing` | Plain-text conventions (same as below) |
| `contentSha256` | SHA-256 hashes of `audio.y`, `video.frames`, `truth.pos` |

### `params` — the scenario exactly as specified

Every field from `mantis_std_specs.m` (`duration`, `fs`, `numNodes`, `ringRadius`, `platform`, `pathType`, `startXY`, `endXY`, `center`, `radius`, `numLoops`, `altitude`, `snrDb`, `noiseType`, `enableDoppler`, `sky`, `fps`, `imageSize`, `fovDeg`, `projection`, `deadNodes`, `seed`, …) plus values the emulator resolved: `sourceType`, `sourceFreq`, `gain`, `navLights`, `camHeight`.

### `nodes`

| Field | Size | Units | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | N × 1 | — | 1 … N |
| `xy` | N × 2 | m | Node ground position |
| `micZ` | scalar | m | Microphone height (0) |
| `camHeight` | scalar | m | Camera height (0.15) |
| `alive` | N × 1 | logical | Node fully online |
| `micAlive`, `camAlive` | N × 1 | logical | Per-sensor status |

### `audio`

| Field | Size | Units | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fs` | scalar | Hz | Sample rate (8000) |
| `t` | T × 1 | s | Sample times, $t_i = (i-1)/f_s$ |
| `y` | T × N | arbitrary, single | **Microphone signal** with noise. Offline mics are all zeros. |
| `yClean` | T × N | arbitrary, single | Same signal before noise (for debugging, not for evaluation) |
| `snrDb`, `noiseType` | — | dB, — | Noise settings |
| `sourceType`, `sourceFreq` | — | —, Hz | Source model (rotor-like, 130 Hz SWIFT / 170 Hz F550) |
| `speedOfSound` | scalar | m/s | 343 |

### `video`

| Field | Size | Units | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frames` | H × W × K × N | uint8 | **Fisheye frames.** `frames(:,:,k,n)` is frame k from node n. Offline cameras are all zeros. |
| `t` | K × 1 | s | Frame times |
| `sampleIdx` | K × 1 | — | 1-based row of `audio.y` captured at the same instant as frame k |
| `fps` | scalar | Hz | Actual frame rate |
| `imageSize` | 1 × 2 | px | [rows cols] |
| `fovDeg`, `projection` | — | deg, — | 185, `equidistant` |
| `fPix` | scalar | px/rad | Focal length |
| `cx`, `cy` | scalar | px | Principal point (image center, 1-based) |
| `camYawDeg` | scalar | deg | Camera mounting yaw (0) |
| `sky`, `gain`, `navLights` | — | — | Rendering settings |

### `truth`

| Field | Size | Units | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `t` | T × 1 | s | Identical to `audio.t` |
| `pos` | T × 3 | m | **UAV position** [x y z] |
| `vel` | T × 3 | m/s | Velocity (numerical derivative of `pos`) |
| `speed` | T × 1 | m/s | Ground-truth speed |
| `attitude` | T × 3 | rad | [yaw pitch roll] actually rendered |
| `rangeToNodes` | T × N | m | Slant range from each camera to the UAV |
| `propDelay` | T × N | s | Source-to-microphone propagation delay (when the emulator provides it) |
| `micRange` | T × N | m | Source-to-microphone distance (when provided) |
| `closestRange`, `closestTime` | N × 1 | m, s | Closest approach per node |
| `camera` | struct | | Per-frame camera truth, below |

`truth.camera` (each K × N unless noted):

| Field | Units | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u`, `v` | px | Image position of the airframe origin (1-based, subpixel) |
| `bbox` | px | K × N × 4, `[uMin vMin width height]`, exact from the renderer |
| `range` | m | Slant range at the frame time |
| `pixelArea` | px | Target coverage after compositing |
| `angularSize` | deg | Apparent angular size of the airframe |
| `inFOV` | logical | Target inside the field of view |

---

## Conventions

**Coordinate frame.** Local field frame with the origin at the ring center on the ground. $x$ and $y$ are horizontal, $z$ is up (height above ground). Azimuth is measured counterclockwise from $+x$.

**Attitude.** `[yaw pitch roll]` in radians, body axes $x$ forward, $y$ left, $z$ up. The body-to-world rotation is

$$R = R_z(\psi)\,R_y(-\theta)\,R_x(\phi)$$

where $\psi$ is yaw (0 means nose along $+x$), $\theta$ is pitch (positive nose up), and $\phi$ is roll (positive right wing down). Attitude is kinematic: the airframe points along its velocity and banks into turns.

**Time alignment.** Frames sit exactly on the audio sample grid, and all nodes are triggered at the same instants, so no resampling is needed:

```matlab
k   = 13;                              % frame 13 (t = 12 s)
i   = video.sampleIdx(k);              % matching audio row
win = i + (-audio.fs/2 : audio.fs/2);  % one second of audio around it
clip = audio.y(win, :);
```

**Camera model.** Each camera looks straight up. A point at zenith angle $\vartheta$ (angle off the optical axis, rad) and azimuth $\varphi$ (rad, counterclockwise from $+x$) lands at

$$r = f\,\vartheta, \qquad u = c_x + r\cos\varphi, \qquad v = c_y - r\sin\varphi$$

where $f$ is `video.fPix` (px/rad), $(c_x, c_y)$ is the principal point (px), and $r$ is the radial distance from the image center (px). So $+x$ points right in the image and $+y$ points up. At 240 px over 185°, one pixel spans about 0.77° (13.5 mrad).

**Indexing.** All indices stored in the files are MATLAB 1-based. The Python loader adds 0-based `video["sample_idx0"]` and `nodes["id0"]`; pixel coordinates stay 1-based, so subtract 1 before indexing a NumPy image.

**Offline nodes (TC06).** An offline microphone is an exact zero signal and an offline camera returns all-zero frames. Treat either as "no data", not as a measurement.

## Loading

**MATLAB**

```matlab
d = load('MANTIS-Std-v1.0.0/TC01_overhead_pass.mat');
plot(d.truth.t, d.truth.rangeToNodes); xlabel('t (s)'); ylabel('range (m)');
imshow(d.video.frames(:,:,13,1));       % node 1 at t = 12 s
```

**Python**

```python
import mantis_std as ms
tc = ms.load_case("MANTIS-Std-v1.0.0/TC01_overhead_pass.mat")
y      = tc["audio"]["y"]          # (192001, 6)
frames = tc["video"]["frames"]     # (240, 240, 25, 6) uint8
pos    = tc["truth"]["pos"]        # (192001, 3)
```

`python mantis_std.py MANTIS-Std-v1.0.0` prints a one-line summary of every case.

---

## Scoring a tracker

Report position error against `truth.pos`, interpolated to your estimate times. The root-mean-square error (RMSE) over $M$ estimates is

$$\mathrm{RMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{M}\sum_{j=1}^{M} \left\lVert \hat{\mathbf{p}}_j - \mathbf{p}(t_j) \right\rVert^2}$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{p}}_j$ is your estimated position (m) at time $t_j$ (s) and $\mathbf{p}(t_j)$ is the true position interpolated from `truth.pos` (m). Report the horizontal and vertical parts separately as well, and state the fraction of the 24 s for which your tracker produced an estimate.

```matlab
truthAtEst = interp1(d.truth.t, d.truth.pos, tEst, 'linear');
err  = xyzEst - truthAtEst;
rmse = sqrt(mean(sum(err.^2, 2), 'omitnan'));
```

```python
ms.score(tc, t_est, xyz_est)   # {'rmse_3d', 'rmse_horizontal', 'rmse_vertical', 'n'}
```

When comparing algorithms, quote the dataset version (for example `MANTIS-Std v1.0.0, TC03`) so results stay tied to the exact data.

---

## Integrity

`index.mat` stores, for each case, the SHA-256 hash of the whole file and of its three key arrays. `verify_standard_testcases()` recomputes them and also checks shapes, time alignment, camera-versus-audio truth consistency, offline-node behavior, and finiteness. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lets anyone check files without MATLAB:

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt                                  # Linux / macOS
Get-FileHash TC01_overhead_pass.mat -Algorithm SHA256        # Windows PowerShell
```

---

## Limitations

These cases inherit every simplification of the v0.2 emulator. They are synthetic and have **not yet been checked against field recordings**; that check is planned work.

- Ideal fisheye lens: no calibrated radial distortion.
- Clean sky only: no trees, buildings, ground clutter, or occlusion in frame.
- No atmospheric absorption of sound and no haze or contrast loss with range.
- Node clocks are perfectly synchronized; real nodes will drift.
- Attitude is kinematic, not a six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) flight model.
- Daylight only in v1.0.0; dusk, night, and cloudy variants are candidates for a later version.

---

## Versioning

The dataset uses semantic versioning in `mantis_std_version.m`:

- **Major**: file layout changes that break existing loaders.
- **Minor**: a case added or a scenario value changed.
- **Patch**: regenerated with a corrected emulator, layout unchanged.

Any edit to `mantis_std_specs.m` requires a version bump so two copies with the same version number always contain the same scenarios.
